sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: speed limits, signaling, lanes, turns, roundabouts, J-turns, U-turns and passing
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The signaling paragraph says to keep signaling until the turn or lane change is complete [A02], while the turn list on the next page says to continue signaling until you begin your turn [A03]; the dossier teaches the stricter first wording and flags the mismatch (verify MN-TRAFFICA-D-SIGNAL).
The left and right turn diagrams, the one-way and two-way turn panels and the roundabout and J-turn drawings were read from their extracted captions only; no fact relies on a picture [A04].
The left-turn-on-red sentence starts at the foot of one page and finishes at the top of the next; the dossier cites the page where the rule begins and records the yield requirement from the following page separately [A03] [A05].
The physical page carrying only the single-lane and two-lane roundabout drawings has no text facts and is not cited.
The ten mph passing allowance is printed twice, in the basic speed law paragraph and again in the passing section; the dossier records it once as a confusable in C2.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.

verification_debt.claim_text: On physical page 30 the Minnesota Driver's Manual (June 2026) says to keep signaling until the turn or lane change is complete, while physical page 31 says to continue signaling until you begin your turn; confirm which wording DVS uses for written test items against an official DVS source.
